item.title: [dailybulletin.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [marinij.com] Wilkinson’s impressive five shutout innings can’t prevent SF Giants from being swept by Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Justice delos Santos
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever. Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts. “Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swe
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever.
Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts.
“Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swept, but the rookie turned in arguably the best start of his short career. In his seventh career appearance, Wilkinson tossed five shutout innings against the NL West champions, collecting a career-high six strikeouts without recording a single walk.
“He was outstanding,” said manager Tony Vitello. “Back at it on the starting deal. To be honest with you, didn’t have a whole lot of trouble to navigate because of how well he threw the ball. … When there was potential for things brewing, he put an end to it.”
“Best one yet since being up,” Wilkinson said. “Really was just throwing all four pitches for strikes today, and that was kind of the mindset going into today. Compete with all four pitches, and I felt like I did a good job with that today.”
Vitello said it’s “too early” to know how Wilkinson could fit into next year’s pitching plans but assessed that Wilkinson is “pretty flexible.” Before Sunday, Wilkinson had pitched five scoreless innings with four strikeouts over his last two outings as a multi-inning reliever. When asked if he prefers starting or relieving, the 23-year-old responded he’s willing to pitch whatever role is needed.
“You want a guy that wants the ball and ain’t scared of those situations,” Vitello said.
Wilkinson certainly didn’t look scared in his first meeting with the reigning back-to-back World Series champions on their home turf. Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Kyle Tucker starting the day on the bench, the Dodgers’ lineup still featured future Hall of Famers Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman and multi-time All-Stars Max Muncy and Teoscar Hernández.
Against Wilkinson, that group couldn’t get anything cooking.
The only threats that the Dodgers posed against Wilkinson were one-out doubles in the second and fifth innings. On both occasions, Wilkinson maneuvered out of trouble and completed five innings for just the second time in his career.
“Especially with this rivalry, it’s awesome and fun to be a small piece of that,” Wilkinson said.
Despite Wilkinson’s efforts, the Dodgers generated enough offense after his departure to complete the dusting.
Tommy Edman tied the game in the bottom of the sixth by turning a 2-2 cutter from Carson Seymour into a solo homer, and Kiké Hernández drove in the go-ahead run in the bottom of the seventh. Muncy, a long-time Giants (64-92) foe, added an RBI single in the bottom of the eighth for insurance.
Jonah Cox, with the use of his elite speed, generated San Francisco’s lone run in the top of the first.
Cox began the afternoon with a leadoff walk, then scrambled to second when the Dodgers’ Jack Dreyer made an errant pickoff throw. Already in scoring position, Cox swiped third with ease, his 14th steal of the season, then scored on a single by Victor Bericoto.
Following Dreyer’s lone inning as the opener, San Francisco couldn’t generate any offense against Los Angeles’ Emmet Sheehan, who allowed one hit over 5 1/3 scoreless innings of long relief with nine strikeouts. Sheehan has been outstanding against the Giants in his career, allowing four runs over 33 1/3 innings
By afternoon’s end, the Giants were reduced to their most inexperienced, anonymous lineup of the season. Rookie Bryce Eldridge missed a third straight game due to a head laceration, and right fielder Jung Hoo Lee was lifted from the game after fouling a pitch off his groin in the top of the sixth. Eldridge is not expected to play on Monday.
Up next
The Giants will return to Oracle Park for their final six games of the regular season, beginning with a three-game set against the Minnesota Twins.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Hints at Possible October Change at Top of Lineup
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order. But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers still expect Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before October, and Dave Roberts made clear Saturday that his first instinct remains to put Ohtani right back atop the batting order.
But the manager is also preparing for the possibility that things don’t go exactly according to plan.
With Ohtani still sidelined and his return date uncertain, Mookie Betts has moved back into the leadoff spot, a familiar home for the former MVP. After Friday night’s two-homer performance against the Giants, Roberts acknowledged that Betts could become an alternative at the top of the order if the Dodgers need to make an adjustment in October.
“Certainly there is uncertainty with Sho, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever. I just think that Mookie is swinging the bat. He’s hit there many times throughout his career. So it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts certainly looked comfortable there Friday. He reached base four times, homered twice and drove in three runs as the Dodgers beat San Francisco 8-2. Long before Ohtani arrived in Los Angeles, Betts was one of baseball’s premier leadoff hitters, so moving him back there isn’t exactly unfamiliar territory.
Roberts has also been encouraged by the quality of Betts’ at-bats during his recent surge.
“I think with Mookie, results drive kind of his demeanor,” Roberts said. “With the results, I think that he is considerably better. He’s not a chase guy anyway, but he’s cut that down considerably. The quality of contact is considerably higher, and then now you’ve got that attitude, that confidence that we’re used to seeing with Mookie.”
For now, Roberts still expects Ohtani to reclaim the leadoff spot once he returns.
“That’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially redirect, react if it’s a left-right situation, or just supplant him back there in the one.”
That leaves the Dodgers with some flexibility. If Ohtani immediately looks like himself, there may be nothing to discuss. But if he needs time to regain his timing after the layoff, the Dodgers don’t have to force the issue at the top of the lineup. Betts has spent most of his career proving he can handle that job.
The Dodgers are also continuing to work Will Smith back toward a normal workload after his own stint on the injured list. Smith was in the lineup Saturday for a second consecutive game, only the third time he has caught back-to-back games since returning.
“I think he’s come along well,” Roberts said. “I think his swing is in a much better spot, getting better, consistent.”
The Dodgers intentionally scheduled Smith for consecutive games this weekend before giving him two days to recover with Monday’s off day included. Roberts said Smith would then play two or three games in the following series.
“I think it’s a good exercise for him,” Roberts said.
Smith’s return matters well beyond his bat. Roberts also pointed to the growing comfort between Smith and Tarik Skubal after their latest game together, saying the pitcher and catcher finally appeared to reach a point of “mutual trust” regarding the game plan and how Skubal wanted to attack hitters.
That relationship will matter considerably if Skubal is asked to pitch deep into October.
The larger picture is that the Dodgers are beginning to have options again. Smith is rebuilding his workload. Betts is swinging the bat with confidence. Ohtani is expected back. And if Ohtani isn’t immediately ready to carry the leadoff responsibilities, the Dodgers have one of the most accomplished leadoff hitters of his generation waiting right behind him.
There are worse backup plans to have in October.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily. The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya. Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily.
The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya.
Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers after Giants start
The timing comes immediately after Skubal’s latest start. He worked five innings against the Giants on Saturday, allowing eight hits, four earned runs and two walks while striking out three.
The Dodgers still won 10-4, with Mookie Betts going 4-for-4 and Will Smith adding a home run. Skubal received the win despite allowing four earned runs in the outing.
The start came during an important stretch for the Dodgers, who are already looking toward their postseason rotation. Skubal has given Los Angeles another frontline option since joining the club from Detroit.
His temporary absence, however, will force the Dodgers to make a short-term adjustment.
Dodgers turn to Emmet Sheehan
Emmet Sheehan is expected to step back into the Dodgers’ pitching plans Sunday. The right-hander provides another option as Los Angeles manages its rotation while Skubal is away.
The Dodgers have enough pitching depth to cover a short absence. Yoshinobu Yamamoto remains in the rotation, while Blake Snell has returned from the injured list.
Los Angeles has also already secured the NL West, giving the club some flexibility with its pitching plans. That could allow the Dodgers to avoid putting extra pressure on Skubal to return immediately.
Still, his availability will matter once the postseason begins. Skubal has been an important part of the Dodgers’ rotation since the trade, and the team will want him ready for October.
For now, the Dodgers will move forward without their ace for the next few days. The focus will be on Skubal’s return timeline and how Los Angeles adjusts its pitching plans in his absence.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Mookie Betts' sudden revival could be Dodgers' secret weapon in securing three-peat
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start. item.content:encoded:
The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start.
Specifically since August 17, he's been one of the best hitters in all of baseball. He leads the Los Angeles Dodgers in all three triple-slash categories (.336/.427/.611), wRC+ (183), home runs (seven), RBI (27), and fWAR (2.0) from that point forward, emerging at a time when the team has gotten all of 71 plate appearances (and a 101 wRC+) from Shohei Ohtani.
Betts isn't a "secret weapon" by traditional standards; his MVP credentials and three World Series rings would certainly beg to differ. But after he struggled mightily a year ago and then followed that up with an even worse encore at the beginning of 2026, having him healthy and in his best groove in years could be the deciding factor in the Dodgers' quest for a three-peat.
Mookie Betts has elevated his own floor and with it, the Dodgers' ceiling
The Dodgers are hardly hurting for production, ranking third in the league in runs scored since mid-August. Even without Ohtani, they can batter opposing pitching staffs with their depth, especially now that Kyle Tucker finally looks interested in participating in this group project.
But more than a rejuvenated Tucker or red-hot Teoscar Hernández, there's something special about Betts in particular getting this hot. He's the fourth-longest tenured player on the roster, surpassed by only Max Muncy and Will Smith among position players. He's been around for each of the three recent championships, posting a cumulative OPS over .800 in those playoff runs.
One of the most selfless superstars you'll ever find, there's a "you go, we go" aura that orbits Betts, especially now that he's reclaimed his rightful spot atop the batting order as Dave Roberts' leadoff hitter. His all-around talents lengthen the lineup to a tremendous degree, something opposing pitchers will really feel once Ohtani is back in the fold.
It's not all perfect, of course. His hard-hit rate even during this hot streak is well below the figures he'd post in his prime, and he's still hitting a few too many balls on the ground. Naturally, all of his expected stats during this stretch fall shy of his actual results, including significant disparities in his slugging percentage (.611 compared to a .458 xSLG) and wOBA (.443 compared to a .374 xwOBA).
Those expected metrics are still leaps and bounds better than we got earlier this season, though, and that's the real takeaway here. Even if Betts can't keep this MVP-caliber charade going through all of October, he's clearly found a more stable baseline level of performance that can still help the Dodgers win.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants. They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula recently made his MLB debut with LA.
He’s had a few very solid moments at the plate, and he’s showcased his impressive plate discipline with an ability to put the ball in play and drive it to the opposite side of the field.
De Paula is still very young, so there’s plenty of time to develop in the coming years, but it’s been a welcome sign thus far in his first handful of MLB action.
Recently, Josue De Paula shared an honest message about dealing with critics to Dodgers reporter Fabian Ardaya.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message
Per Ardaya, here is what Josue De Paula had to say about critics calling out his defense:
“I know that’s a big area of improvement for me,” said De Paula. “I know I got a lot of hate on it. I’m that type: if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. So I’m gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon. It’s gonna take some time.”
Even manager Dave Roberts said that De Paula still has a lot of development to do in the outfield, but it’s been clear De Paula’s defense isn’t the reason he’s in the show.
Ardaya notes that De Paula could have a full-time role with the Dodgers if he shores up his defensive ability:
“The list of helpful voices kept growing over the first 10 days of De Paula’s big-league career. His bat could be special, but De Paula’s path to impacting the 2027 Dodgers becomes a lot easier if he proves he can handle the corner outfield. Mookie Betts, a six-time Gold Glove winner in right field, gave him pointers on how to shag fly balls. Manager Dave Roberts, who spent 10 years patrolling big-league outfields, goes out of his way to ensure De Paula emphasizes the details.”
With all the stars on the Dodgers roster, De Paula’s development is in good hands.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Pitch Offloads Mark Vientos to Pirates
Josue De Paula’s Rookie Campaign Thus Far
Josue De Paula has played in just 10 games for LA, and across his first 38 MLB plate appearances, he’s batted .286 with 10 walks, eight hits, six runs, one home run, and 3 doubles.
Those are very solid numbers to start your MLB career, and especially as a top prospect.
Here is some of De Paula’s prospect bio, per MiLB.com:
“De Paula draws comparisons to a slightly smaller but more athletic version of Yordan Alvarez, thanks to his precocious combination of swing decisions and exit velocities. He offered at just 14 percent of pitches outside the strike zone last season — by comparison, Juan Soto led the Majors with a 16 percent rate — and is supremely comfortable working deep counts in order to find pitches he can punish.”
Yordan Alvarez? The frontrunner for 2026 AL MVP? Not a bad comparison. The future looks bright for Josue De Paula thus far.

item.title: [Yardbarker] 'Wouldn’t Have Won the World Series': Shohei Ohtani’s Impact on Dodgers Runs Deeper Than Expected as Dave Roberts Reveals Why
item.dc:creator: Srijanee Chakraborty
item.description: Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score. It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto. According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for t
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score.
It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for the entire team. It did not go unnoticed by the players.
Roberts recalled on the611podcast that Dodgers veteran Mookie Betts also felt the same.
“Mookie told me a couple of years ago, ‘Doc, we wouldn’t have won the World Series if it wasn’t for Shohei and Yamamoto’. And his point was the discipline that they had every single day,” said Roberts on the podcast.
“How they work with intention every single day, because what that made, it raised the level even higher for our guys. Yamamoto’s day-to-day is three to four hours of intentionality to prepare to throw a bullpen. Shohei is the same way. Roki is getting there, but his culture- that’s what they do.”
The Dodgers signed Ohtani and Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season.
Ohtani signed the historic 10-year, $700 million contract, while Yamamoto agreed to a massive 12-year, $325 million deal. They proved that every million spent was worth it, as the Dodgers became the World Series champion in 2024 and again in 2025.
Ohtani’s three-homer, 10-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the NLCS, leading to the World Series, is one for the history books. In Game 2 of the 2024 World Series, Ohtani suffered a partial dislocation in his left shoulder while trying to steal a base. But showing incredible toughness, he returned in Game 3 to play against the New York Yankees.
It does not happen without intentionality, and Ohtani’s whole regimen is driven by it. Shotime runs by the clock; from sleeping to bullpen sessions, everything has a fixed schedule. He is Roberts’ “easiest player to manage.”
Last season, Ohtani finished Game 3 of the World Series by reaching base a record-setting 9 times, hitting 2 doubles and 2 homers. The two-way phenom ended the championship batting .333, with 3 homers and 5 RBIs.
Yamamoto was equally impressive.
During the 2024 Fall Classic, Yamamoto threw a one-hit, one-run game, pitching for six innings. In the following edition, he threw in three games and gave up 2 runs to the Toronto Blue Jays, logging a 1.02 ERA.
“When you’re talking about winning 11 games in October, I couldn’t believe more [that] it’s about people, and players you can bet on,” Roberts said on the podcast.
Ohtani and Yamamoto are the players Roberts bet on. Their success is defined by the discipline they rigorously maintain.
When Yamamoto arrived at the Dodgers clubhouse, he brought his own regimen that influenced others.
He relies on flexibility to generate momentum rather than brute strength. Apart from taking bullpen sessions like clockwork, Yamamoto also practices javelin throwing.
He follows a routine designed by his personal trainer and guru, Osamu Yada. Yamamoto also famously keeps a notebook in the dugout to jot down observations from the game. All these habits work together to make him successful.
Roberts also revealed how the presence of these Japanese players influenced the Americans.
“So now, when you get younger players that we have, or even American players that are veterans, they’re like, they’re doing it this intentional, this precise, and that’s the thing that, as a manager, I love,” noted Roberts.
“Because you don’t know where games are gonna go. Games are gonna get hot, and the pressure’s gonna get there. But you have to be able to default to kind of what you know. And that’s what, again, in baseball, can kind of default to doing things the right way.”
And to the Dodgers’ credit, they did not try to ignore the vastly unfamiliar culture. Rather, they chose to learn from it. Perhaps that mentality is what makes them champions.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, on Sunday and improved to 96-60 on the year. They completed the series sweep of the divisional rivals and notched their fourth-straight win (and 14th of the last 17).
After Jack Dreyer took the start and allowed an earned run in the first inning, Emmet Sheehan pitched the next 5.1 frames and stole the show on the mound. He struck out nine, allowed one hit, one walk and no earned runs.
Offensively, Teoscar Hernndez, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy and Josue De Paula each had a two-hit game. De Paula was 5-for-10 over the course of the series, just the first of hopefully many more at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the eventual victory, southpaw Tarik Skubal unfortunately had to be placed on the bereavement list. As he deals with his personal matter, it is likely that he will still make one more start (he is next scheduled for Sept. 26) before the postseason.
In other news, manager Dave Roberts made a somewhat surprising admission regarding superstar Mookie Betts. After hitting just .235 before the All-Star break, Betts has completely turned things around and looks like a more familiar version of himself, hitting .322 in his last 30 games.
"I couldn't tell you that I saw this," Roberts said on Saturday regarding Betts' turnaround. "But I just felt that he was stronger. He's worked hard on that. He looks great. He's not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great."
Finally, a Dodgers pitcher was demoted as part of the four-player roster move made on Sunday. The right-hander has an impressive 1.32 ERA across 26 games (27.1 innings) at the Triple-A level, but in 11 appearances with the Dodgers this season, he has an 8.10 ERA across 10 innings of work.

item.title: [sbsun.com] Emmet Sheehan strengthens postseason case as Dodgers sweep Giants
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece. Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Breaks Down Viral Clip With Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani. De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates. Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually g
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula went viral Friday after doing a double take following a high five with Shohei Ohtani.
De Paula, who came up to replace Ohtani upon the MVP’s move to the injured list, had a huge game from the No. 9 spot on Friday, going 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI. His second run of the game came off of a Mookie Betts homer, and he followed the All-Star through the dugout giving high fives to his teammates.
Upon reaching Ohtani in the line, De Paula casually gave him a high five before doing a double take with a surprised look on his face.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game,” De Paula said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez. “He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait.”
De Paula is just 21 years old, and is already making quite the impact with the Dodgers. Through nine games with the team so far, De Paula has a .929 OPS with one homer and seven RBIs. His underlying numbers look great across the board, as he strikes out at an extremely low clip while maintaining fantastic quality of contact in his small MLB sample size.
When Will Shohei Ohtani Be Back?
Ohtani hasn’t played since Sept. 7, as he is nursing a biceps issue. He is slowly returning to baseball activities, and began running the bases prior to Saturday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Following Saturday’s game, manager Dave Roberts revealed he could return against the San Diego Padres in the Dodgers’ next series, which begins on Tuesday. His return would be huge for the Dodgers just before the postseason, and while he may not be able to pitch in October, he will play a huge role at the top of the Dodgers’ lineup as they aim to win their third World Series in a row.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.
“Yeah, no doubt. Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do,” Skubal said. “You know, they… pic.twitter.com/4TUdrQqgH8
"Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do," Skubal said after the game.
In his nine starts with the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the MLB trade deadline, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 4-2 record with 60 strikeouts in 55 innings.
The Dodgers took a 2-0 lead on a first-inning RBI double by Max Muncy and Mookie Betts hitting a run-scoring single in the second. But San Francisco tied the score in the third on a 2-run homer from Victor Bericoto, hitting a fastball left in the very middle of the strike zone by Skubal.
The two teams then traded runs during the third through fifth innings, resulting in a 4-4 tie, before the Dodgers pulled away on a 2-run hit by Tommy Edman and RBI single from Miguel Rojas. In the following inning, the Dodgers added three more runs with Will Smith driving in a run and Josue De Paula hitting a 2-run single.
To fill Skubal's spot on the active roster, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts, taking over for opener Jack Dreyer in the Dodgers' 3-1 win. In his previous two starts before being optioned, Sheehan allowed one run over 11 2/3 innings with 15 strikeouts.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Mookie Betts makes bold statement about recent success
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Mookie Betts continued his torrid stretch at the plate in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Saturday night, going 4-for-4 with three doubles, two RBI and a walk. item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts continued his torrid stretch at the plate in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants on Saturday night, going 4-for-4 with three doubles, two RBI and a walk.
The big performance came after Betts hit two home runs in Friday’s series opener at Dodger Stadium as part of a 3-for-4 effort at the plate. He is now 10-for-12 with five extra-base hits, five RBI, five runs scored and three walks over his last three games.
“Yeah, I mean, this is it,” Betts said when asked if this is the version of himself that he has been chasing. “I know I’m still capable of it; it’s in there somewhere. So just got to keep on rolling, keep on, like I said, laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”
Betts has been one of the Dodgers’ hottest hitters over the past month after struggling offensively for much of the season. He is hitting a stellar .359/.449/.652 with nine doubles, six home runs and 21 RBI over his last 28 games.
Betts attributed his recent success to seeing the ball better and his swing finally being in a good spot.
“Oh, I think it’s both,” Betts began. “Swing is a little more consistent, hitting balls in the middle of the zone hard, and able to take balls. So that’s the name of the game. Hit strikes hard and take balls.”
Betts has consistently tinkered with his swing this year and is now reaping the rewards of his hard work. His resurgence couldn’t have come at a better time for the Dodgers, who are playing out the final week of the regular season before beginning what they hope will be a deep playoff run.
Dave Roberts surprised by Mookie Betts
Roberts has stood by Betts all season, but even he didn’t expect the eight-time All-Star to bounce back in such a big way.
“You know, I didn’t,” Roberts admitted. “I couldn’t tell you that I saw this, but I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.
“I think for me, it’s just trying to keep him confident. His teammates have poured into him, and again, it’s as good as we’ve seen him over a consistent period in a while.”

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Is it still a rivalry? item.content:encoded:
Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: Repeating the trend of these series’ first two games, the Dodgers didn’t take the lead until the second half of the game—this time keeping their scoring to nearly the minimum needed to overcome the Giants, sweeping their rivals with a 3-1 victory that relied heavily on Emmet Sheehan’s work as the bulk man, following Jack Dreyer. Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win Emmet Sheehan’s outstanding work as a follower allowed the Dodgers to beat the Giants with
item.content:encoded:
Repeating the trend of these series’ first two games, the Dodgers didn’t take the lead until the second half of the game—this time keeping their scoring to nearly the minimum needed to overcome the Giants, sweeping their rivals with a 3-1 victory that relied heavily on Emmet Sheehan’s work as the bulk man, following Jack Dreyer.
Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win
Emmet Sheehan’s outstanding work as a follower allowed the Dodgers to beat the Giants with just three runs
Without putting the ball in play, the Giants placed a man on third in the opening inning, manufacturing a run partially thanks to Dreyer’s loose grip on the running game. Leadoff hitter Jonah Cox earned a walk as Dreyer struggled to locate his heater, moved to second on an errant pickoff attempt, and aggressively stole third—hardly a surprise for a rookie with 13 stolen bases in just 140 plate appearances. Cox was driven in by a Jonah Bericoto single, a run that would loom large given the effectiveness of both Sheehan and Giants starter Matt Wilkinson.
Deceptive with his low-90s fastball that gets terrific results, Giants starter Matt Wilkinson didn’t encounter many problems holding the Dodgers scoreless through five innings of work. Only twice did Wilkinson need to strand one-out doubles, but on both occasions with minimal stress. That success was at least partially owed to a lefty-heavy lineup—three of the four outs Wilkinson recorded with a runner in scoring position came against a left-handed hitter, but then again, one of the doubles came from Josue De Paula, so we mustn’t read too much into it.
As soon as Wilkinson got the hook, though, the Dodgers would tie the game in the bottom of the sixth, thanks to a solo shot from Tommy Edman off Carson Seymour. Traditionally a better power hitter from the right side, Edman was looking in the whole way and crushed one all the way out to the Giants’ bullpen.
The only reason why the Dodgers were able to tie the score with just one swing was the fact that Sheehan matched Wilkinson pitch for pitch and then some. Overall, few players have improved their case for a significant postseason role over the past couple of weeks with the Dodgers quite like Sheehan, a new pitcher since his return following a one-month stint in Triple-A. Pitching as brilliantly as he did in two September starts, Sheehan completely shut down the Giants’ lineup through 5.1 innings, enjoying great success with a curveball that induced six whiffs on 12 swings, leading him to strike out nine batters.
Proving Wilkinson and his difficult-to-pick-up fastball were the problem, the Dodgers’ offense scored again in the seventh—they took the lead thanks to a Kiké Hernández RBI single after De Paula and Max Muncy set the table despite an unfavorable matchup against the southpaw.
Mookie Betts nearly put this game to bed, but what would’ve been a two-out, three-run bomb died at the wall, leaving the score at 2-1. The Dodgers would still find a way to provide a little cushion to Tanner Scott in the ninth inning, adding one more run in the bottom of the eighth thanks to a Max Muncy two-out RBI single.
Game particulars
- Home run— Tommy Edman (7)
- WP—Kris Bubic (4-2): 0.2 IP, 1 strikeout
- LP— Sam Hentges (1-7): 0.1 IP, 3 hits, 1 run
- SV Tanner Scott (23): 1 IP, 1 walk, 1 strikeout
Up next
It’s a rare off day at home for the Dodgers before the San Diego Padres come into town on Tuesday hoping to clinch their playoff berth. Although neither team has announced their starters, based on the current schedule, the first game of that series would pit Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray against each other. It’s a standard 7:10 p.m. (PT).

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Manager Makes Surprise Admission About Mookie Betts' Resurgence

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts led off in manager Dave Roberts' lineup for the third consecutive game Sunday against the San Francisco Giants. Betts looks immovable right now, especially on the heels of a game in which he reached base five times. He collected three doubles, a single and a walk in the Dodgers' 10-4 win on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
Betts' September surge marks an abrupt change from the five months that came before.
Through the end of August, Betts' .701 OPS ranked 123rd out of 163 major league hitters with at least 400 plate appearances. Since Sept. 1, his OPS was an outstanding 1.287 entering Sunday, trailing only Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz among 181 qualified hitters this month.
"I couldn’t tell you that I saw this,” Roberts said Saturday, referring to Betts' dramatic turnaround. “But I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.”
The Dodgers will have a choice to make if and when Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. Ostensibly he'll go back to the leadoff spot again, though his health — and Betts' resurgence — are at least making it a conversation.
For the Dodgers, it's a good problem to have at the right time.
At 33, Betts is facing many of the same questions the Dodgers' other 30-and-over stars face anytime their performance slips. Has age caught up to them? Can they maintain their performance through the end of October? Do the Dodgers need a younger player to take their place in order to repeat as World Series champions?
The questions apply to Miguel Rojas (37), Freddie Freeman (36), Max Muncy (35), Kiké Hernández (34), Teoscar Hernández (33), Tommy Edman (31) and Ohtani (31), as well as Betts.
Professional athletes are famously the last to know when their physical skills are no longer enough to justify their roster spot. Take it with a grain of salt, but Betts isn't worried about his ability to maintain his current stretch of play.
“I mean this is it,” Betts said of his recent form. “I know I’m still capable of it, it’s in there somewhere. So, just gotta keep on rolling, keep on laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”

A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers kept right fielder Kyle Tucker out of their lineup for Sunday’s game after he exited Saturday’s win early.
Tucker fouled a ball off of his shin Saturday, and left the game shortly after. Manager Dave Roberts expected Tucker to return to the lineup Sunday, but the outfielder clearly isn’t fit to participate.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers are running a bullpen day on Sunday, and could have a few players fill in if needed. Jack Dreyer is getting the ball first for the Dodgers, making his second start of the season. He has a 3.19 ERA through 63 appearances with 68 strikeouts in 59.1 innings pitched.
Emmet Sheehan has a locker at Dodger Stadium as well, and could handle bulk for LA on Sunday.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
Shortstop Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot for the Dodgers, and center fielder Tommy Edman shoots up the order to bat second. Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez bats third, and first baseman Freddie Freeman serves as the cleanup hitter.
Miguel Rojas enters the lineup as the second baseman and No. 5 hitter, and third baseman Max Muncy slides down the order to the No. 6 spot. Josue De Paula remains the team’s designated hitter, and following him are left fielder Kiké Hernandez and catcher Hunter Feduccia to round out the Dodgers’ lineup.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Giants
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Tommy Edman, CF
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Freddie Freeman, 1B
5. Miguel Rojas, 2B
6. Max Muncy, 3B
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Kiké Hernandez, LF
9. Hunter Feduccia, C
Who is Starting for the Giants?
On the mound for the Giants is left-hander Matt WIlkinson, who will be making his seventh appearance of the year. He has a 4.58 ERA through 19.2 innings pitched, striking out 12 batters durign that time.
The rookie struggled in his first stint as a starter, transitioning to relief for his last two appearances and holding his opponents scoreless.
The Dodgers will look to break his scoreless streak in Sunday’s game, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [cbssports.com] Dodgers eye sweep of Giants behind surging Mookie Betts

Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers. Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearan
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers will continue getting their house in order when they face the San Francisco Giants on Sunday afternoon to complete the Dodgers' next-to-last home series of the regular season.
Los Angeles will use a bullpen game Sunday when it seeks a three-game series sweep, while the Giants will send left-hander Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 4.58 ERA) to the mound for his first appearance against the Dodgers.
Los Angeles has a lot of uncertainty heading into its 14th consecutive playoff appearance -- including the rotation because Blake Snell is working through groin discomfort -- while the offense has Shohei Ohtani (biceps inflammation, knee soreness) and Andy Pages (left hand fracture) nearing a return from the injured list.
The revival of Mookie Betts, along with the arrival of Josue De Paula from the minor leagues, has brought renewed energy after a mid-summer swoon.
The Dodgers still do not have a return date for Ohtani, with Betts the latest to claim the star's leadoff spot. Betts had two home runs among his three hits as the leadoff hitter Friday, then returned to the top spot Saturday and went 4-for-4 with three doubles and a walk. He has 10 hits over his past three games.
"The main thing is doing it when it counts," Betts said. "So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up (offensively)."
Betts had an RBI single in the second inning and an RBI double in the fourth Saturday as the Dodgers earned a 10-4 victory over the Giants.
"He's not a chase guy anyway, but he's cut that down considerably," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "The quality of contact is considerably higher. And then now you've got that attitude, that confidence, that we're used to seeing with Mookie."
The Dodgers' Will Smith also is rounding into form after missing three months with neck inflammation. Smith returned at the start of September and has three home runs over his past nine games, including one in each of the past two games.
Smith started consecutive games Friday and Saturday for the third time since he returned, although he is expected to be used off the bench, if at all, on Sunday.
The Giants have their own injury concerns. Ace Logan Webb was the latest to see his season end early, due to a blister on his right middle finger.
On Saturday, first baseman Bryce Eldridge missed his second consecutive game with a head laceration. The 6-foot-7 rookie bumped his head on a low overhang at the team hotel.
"He's still feeling the implications of that deal," Giants manager Tony Vitello said Saturday. "It's kind of a weird spot in the hotel. I checked it out. (Friday) it was a little bit more about just his comfort. But now, stemming from last night and this morning, those guys have been monitoring him like crazy. Just some lingering effects."
Giants rookie Victor Bericoto hit a two-run home run Saturday in his second game since returning from the injured list and now has five homers in 35 career games.
With a win Sunday, the Dodgers can earn their first three-game sweep over the Giants since April 2024. Los Angeles leads the season series 5-4, with one game remaining in L.A. and three games at San Francisco to end the regular season.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers doblegan Giants
Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
El novato dominicano Josué De Paula pega sencillo impulsador de 2 carreras, anota dos y recibe dos bases por bolas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Notes: LA Promotes Outfielder, Shohei Ohtani Injury Update, Teoscar Hernandez Trade?
